milestone: Immutable CPU Bool arrays and numeric/Bool/record mapping

implementation.types: Homogeneous [Bool] arrays; named/anonymous maps between Bool, the six CPU numeric families and finite records
implementation.layout: Canonical one-byte values 0/1, rank-one owned descriptors, private task identity distinct from scalar Bool and other arrays
implementation.ownership: Invocation-owned arrays with checked descriptor range and complete canonical-byte validation at worker handoff and CLI display
implementation.evaluation: Sequential map callbacks, preserved length identity, skipped empty callback bodies, checked indexing and no implicit numeric conversion
implementation.cancellation: Byte validation polls every 256 elements; failed/cancelled retained copies publish no partial output
implementation.limits: CPU only; Bool tensors, Bool-array record fields, nested arrays and collection-valued callbacks remain gated

coverage: Six numeric predicate and Bool-to-numeric encoder families
Named/anonymous Bool maps, Bool/record maps, nested captures and imported helpers
Literals/contextual empties, length, integer indexing, branches and immutable inputs
Direct/nested workers, repeated cached observations, source settlement and scheduler destruction
One/four workers; array lengths 0,1,257,4097 and exact canonical byte representation
Cancellation/deadlines/admission, malformed descriptors and bytes 2/255, allocation failures
Failed/cancelled copies preserve destination buffers; scheduler/invocation owners settle
Bounds and callback arithmetic faults, recovery, and rejected-artifact preservation
CLI limits/all output, full validation of hidden lanes and retained display after settlement
Documentation example compiled and executed in all four variants
Prior numeric/record/array/Bool/compiler/task suites and selected Metal regressions
